'''Jameer Lamar Nelson Sr.'''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/rpp//q//pid/39174/_//players.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191209092614/https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/rpp//q//pid/39174/_//players.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 9, 2019|title=Jameer Lamar NELSON (USA)|website=[[FIBA]].com|access-date=January 26, 2020}}</ref> (born February 9, 1982) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who currently serves as the executive vice president of basketball operations for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball|Saint Joseph's Hawks]], where he was named [[List of U.S. men's college basketball national player of the year awards|national college player of the year]] in 2004. Drafted 20th overall in the [[2004 NBA draft]], Nelson spent the first ten years of his NBA career with the [[Orlando Magic]]. In 2009, he was named an [[NBA All-Star|All-Star]] and made an appearance in the [[2009 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] with the Magic. He also played in the NBA for the [[Dallas Mavericks]], [[Boston Celtics]], [[Denver Nuggets]], [[New Orleans Pelicans]], and [[Detroit Pistons]].

==High school career==
{{Expand section|date=June 2025}}
Nelson attended [[Chester High School (Chester, Pennsylvania)|Chester High School]] in [[Chester, Pennsylvania]] and was a letterman in basketball. In 2000, he helped lead his team to the PIAA AAAA State championship.{{cn|date=June 2025}}

==College career==
Nelson began his play at [[Saint Joseph's University]] in the 2000–01 season. He had a breakout freshman season in which he was named unanimous National Freshman of the Year. During his junior season in [[2002–03 Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball team|2002–03]], he averaged 19.7 points per game, 5.1 rebounds per game, and 4.7 assists per game. He declared for the [[2003 NBA draft]], but later decided to remain for his senior season.{{citation needed|date=June 2025}}

Nelson led the [[Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball|Saint Joseph's Hawks]] to a 27–0 regular season record in 2003–04. The Hawks' first loss came in the [[2004 Atlantic 10 men's basketball tournament|Atlantic 10 tournament]] to Xavier. Nelson and junior guard [[Delonte West]] formed what was largely considered the nation's best backcourt, helping the Hawks earn a #1 seed in the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA tournament]]. They advanced to the [[Elite Eight]] and were within seconds of the [[Final Four]] before [[Oklahoma State Cowboys]]' [[John Lucas III]] hit a [[three-point field goal|three-pointer]] with only a few seconds remaining (after the make, Nelson dribbled up the court and had a chance to tie the game, but his 15-foot shot fell short). Saint Joseph's finished with a 30–2 record, the best in the university's history. Nelson averaged 20.6 points, 5.3 assists, and 2.9 steals per game. He received the [[Lowe's Senior CLASS Award]] his final year, recognizing him as the nation's top senior men's basketball player. He left the Hawks as the best player in the program's history, as its all-time leader in scoring (2,094 points), assists (714), and steals (256). Nelson's number was retired by the university on April 23, 2004.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sjuhawks.com/sports/ath/roster/jameer-nelson/2418|title=Jameer Nelson - 2013-14 - Athletics|website=Saint Joseph's University|language=en|access-date=2020-04-26}}</ref>

Because of his extraordinary accomplishments as a senior, Nelson won the 2004 [[John R. Wooden Award|Wooden Award]], the 2004 [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Award]], the 2004 [[Bob Cousy Award]], the Rupp Trophy, the [[Oscar Robertson Trophy]] and many more accolades, including being featured on the cover of Sports Illustrated. Nelson was the first [[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] athlete to be on the cover of the magazine since [[Mark Macon]] in 1988.{{citation needed|date=June 2025}}

==Professional career==

===Orlando Magic (2004–2014)===
[[File:Jameer Nelson 5417138917.jpg|thumb|left|Nelson spent 11 seasons with Orlando from 2004 to 2014.]]
[[File:Jameer Nelson and Dwight Howard.jpg|thumb|right|Nelson with then Magic teammate [[Dwight Howard]].]]
Nelson was selected with the 20th overall pick in the [[2004 NBA draft]] by the [[Denver Nuggets]], and was subsequently traded to the [[Orlando Magic]] for a 2005 first-round draft pick. Though many speculated he would be a top 10 pick, he fell to number 20, and the Magic were able to acquire both Nelson and [[Dwight Howard]] in the same draft.

As a rookie, Nelson served as the primary backup to the Magic's All-Star point guard [[Steve Francis]]. Due to Nelson's impressive play, the Magic moved Francis to shooting guard to make room for Nelson to start at point guard.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2005/03/21/orlando-skiles-a-perfect-fit/ | work=ChicagoTribune.com | first=Sam | last=Smith | title=Orlando, Skiles a perfect fit | date=March 21, 2005 | access-date=March 21, 2005 | url-status=live | archive-url=http://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/20050323140311/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2005-03-21/sports/0503210182_1_magic-history-scott-skiles-johnny-davis | archive-date=March 23, 2005 }}</ref> He was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]], and garnered [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award|Rookie of the Year]] consideration.<ref>{{cite news | url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2005-04-14/news/0504150030_1_rub-jameer-nelson-ast | work=ChicagoTribune.com | title=Jameer Nelson, Orlando (30 pts., 8 ast., 5 rbs.) Is... | date=April 14, 2005 | access-date=April 14, 2005 | url-status=dead | archive-url=http://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/20050414143105/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2005-04-14/news/0504150030_1_rub-jameer-nelson-ast | archive-date=April 14, 2005 }}</ref>

On February 22, 2006, the Magic dealt Francis to the [[New York Knicks]], paving the way for Nelson to become the long-term starting point guard of Orlando.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2339941|title=Magic deal Francis to Knicks for Penny, Ariza|date=February 22, 2006|website=ESPN.com|access-date=May 9, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180329005647/http://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2339941|archive-date=March 29, 2018}}</ref> Nelson's play improved with the mid-season trade of Francis, finishing the season with averages of 14.6 points and 5 assists per game on 48.3% field goal shooting.

The [[2006–07 NBA season|following year]], Nelson helped lead the Magic back into the postseason for the first time since 2003. He averaged 14.3 points, 3 rebounds, and 3.3 assists per game during the NBA playoffs, however the Magic were ultimately swept by the top-seeded Detroit Pistons in the first round.

During the 2008 All-Star weekend Slam Dunk Contest, Nelson assisted teammate [[Dwight Howard]] on several of his dunks, including the famous Superman dunk. [[2007–08 NBA season|That year]], the Magic once again made the playoffs, defeating the Toronto Raptors in the first round before falling to the Pistons in the second round. He averaged 16.2 points, 4.7 assists and 4.1 rebounds per game through the playoffs, helping Orlando to their first playoff series win in 12 years.

[[File:Jameer Nelson.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Nelson taking a shot over [[Antawn Jamison]] of the [[Washington Wizards]].]]
Nelson set career highs in points, steals, and shooting percentages during the [[2008–09 NBA season]]. He, along with teammates Dwight Howard and [[Rashard Lewis]], was selected to the [[2009 NBA All-Star Game]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3870364|title=Hornets' West an All-Star; voters snub Carmelo|date=January 29, 2009|website=ESPN.com|access-date=May 9, 2018}}</ref> However, a torn [[Glenoid labrum|labrum]] in his right shoulder forced him to miss the game. At the time of the injury, Nelson was averaging 16.7 points and 5.4 assists per game.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/2009/news/02/03/magic.nelson.20090203.ap/index.html Magic's Nelson optimistic about playing again this season]</ref> After a four-month recovery, Nelson returned during the [[2009 NBA Finals]], sharing point guard duties with [[Rafer Alston]] as the Magic lost to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in five games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/finals2009|title=2009 NBA Finals|website=NBA.com}}</ref>

On November 16, Nelson suffered a torn meniscus in his left knee, and had [[arthroscopic surgery]] to repair his knee.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=291116019|title=Bobcats vs. Magic - Game Recap - November 16, 2009 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=May 9, 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170321083434/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=291116019|archive-date=March 21, 2017}}</ref> He returned to action on December 21.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=291221019|title=Jazz vs. Magic - Game Recap - December 21, 2009 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=May 9, 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170321083806/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=291221019|archive-date=March 21, 2017}}</ref> Nelson and the Magic again surged into the playoffs with their third straight [[Southeast Division (NBA)|Southeast Division title]], sweeping the Charlotte Bobcats and Atlanta Hawks before falling to the Boston Celtics in six games in the Eastern Conference Finals. He averaged 19 points and 4.8 assists per game in Orlando's 14 playoff games.

[[File:Jameer Nelson pump fake cropped.jpg|thumb|upright|right|Nelson getting ready to take a shot against [[Richard Jefferson]] of the [[San Antonio Spurs]].]]
On March 18, 2011, Nelson made a game winning buzzer beater against the Denver Nuggets to secure an 85–82 victory for Orlando.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jameer Nelson drains 3 at buzzer as Magic prevail late|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/310318019|publisher=ESPN|agency=Associated Press|access-date=April 10, 2011|date=March 18, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121106091434/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?id=310318019|archive-date=November 6, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Jameer Nelson Hits the Game-Winner|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sC2gIOD6G3Q|work=YouTube.com|access-date=June 2, 2013|date=March 19, 2011|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160307053814/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sC2gIOD6G3Q|archive-date=March 7, 2016}}</ref> On April 10, 2011, Nelson's last-second three-pointer was ruled "no basket", and the Magic lost to the Chicago Bulls 102–99.<ref>{{cite web|title=Derrick Rose scores 39 as Bulls thwart Magic to hit 60-win plateau|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/310410019|publisher=ESPN|agency=Associated Press|access-date=April 29, 2011|date=April 10, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110425065358/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?id=310410019|archive-date=April 25, 2011}}</ref>

Nelson and [[Dwight Howard]], who were close friends since their rookie seasons, were on opposite sides of a trade that sent Rashard Lewis to Washington in exchange for [[Gilbert Arenas]] (Nelson considered Lewis one of the team's leaders while Howard reportedly pushed management into making the trade).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/wizards-insider/post/wizards-rashard-lewis-on-dwight-howard-situation-they-cant-focus-on-just-being-a-basketball-team/2011/12/12/gIQAahf4pO_blog.html|title=Wizards' Rashard Lewis on Dwight Howard situation: 'They can't focus on just being a basketball team'|first=Michael|last=Lee|date=December 12, 2011|website=washingtonpost.com|access-date=May 9, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170410220122/https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/wizards-insider/post/wizards-rashard-lewis-on-dwight-howard-situation-they-cant-focus-on-just-being-a-basketball-team/2011/12/12/gIQAahf4pO_blog.html|archive-date=April 10, 2017}}</ref> Their relationship was further strained when Howard publicly stated his desire to play with a superstar point guard like [[Deron Williams]] or [[Chris Paul]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://articles.orlandosentinel.com/2013-03-06/sports/os-magic-heat-news-0306-20130306_1_nelson-and-howard-dwight-howard-jameer-nelson|title=Orlando Magic: Rashard Lewis, Jameer Nelson fire back at Dwight Howard for his comments|website=orlandosentinel.com|access-date=May 9, 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170321082146/http://articles.orlandosentinel.com/2013-03-06/sports/os-magic-heat-news-0306-20130306_1_nelson-and-howard-dwight-howard-jameer-nelson|archive-date=March 21, 2017}}</ref> and was reportedly the driving force behind the firing of coach [[Stan Van Gundy]]. Howard eventually forced a trade to the Lakers in the 2012 offseason. Despite this, Nelson re-signed with the Magic on a three-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic finalize new 3-year contract with Jameer Nelson|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2012/07/16/orlando-magic-finalize-new-3-year-contract-with-jameer-nelson/|work=OrlandoSentinel.com|access-date=July 16, 2012|date=July 16, 2012|last=Robbins|first=Josh|url-status=live|archive-url=http://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/20120718133306/http://articles.orlandosentinel.com/2012-07-16/sports/os-orlando-magic-jameer-nelson-0717-20120716_1_jameer-nelson-orlando-magic-magic-officials|archive-date=July 18, 2012}}</ref>

On February 23, 2014, Nelson scored his 8020th point, passing Shaquille O'Neal for fourth place on the Magic's all-time scoring list.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140223/ORLTOR/gameinfo.html|title=Magic at Raptors|website=nba.com|access-date=May 9, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161101080508/http://www.nba.com/games/20140223/ORLTOR/gameinfo.html|archive-date=November 1, 2016}}</ref>

On June 30, 2014, he was waived by the Magic after 10 seasons with the team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-waive-jameer-nelson|title=Orlando Magic Waive Jameer Nelson - Orlando Magic|website=nba.com|access-date=May 9, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161013152846/http://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-waive-jameer-nelson/|archive-date=October 13, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/press-release-magic-waive-jameer-nelson|title=Press Release: Magic Waive Jameer Nelson - Orlando Magic|website=nba.com|access-date=May 9, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171101123232/http://www.nba.com/magic/press-release-magic-waive-jameer-nelson/|archive-date=November 1, 2017}}</ref>

===Dallas Mavericks (2014)===
[[File:Jameer Nelson Mavs cropped.jpg|thumb|left|Nelson spent the first 23 games of the 2014–15 season with Dallas.]]
On July 24, 2014, Nelson signed a two-year, $5.6 million contract with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavs-sign-former-star-jameer-nelson/|title=Mavs Sign Former All-Star Jameer Nelson|date=July 24, 2014|work=mavs.com|access-date=July 24, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140725084647/http://www.mavs.com/mavs-sign-former-star-jameer-nelson/|archive-date=July 25, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/234413/Jameer-Nelson-Finalizes-Two-Year-$56M-Deal-With-Mavericks|title=Jameer Nelson Finalizes Two-Year, $5.6M Deal With Mavericks|date=July 24, 2014|work=RealGM.com|access-date=July 24, 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140726193016/http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/234413/Jameer-Nelson-Finalizes-Two-Year-$56M-Deal-With-Mavericks|archive-date=July 26, 2014}}</ref> He appeared in 23 games for the Mavericks and averaged 7.3 points and 4.1 assists per game.

===Boston Celtics (2014–2015)===
On December 18, 2014, Nelson was traded, along with [[Jae Crowder]], [[Brandan Wright]], a 2015 first-round pick, a 2016 second-round pick and a $12.9 million trade exception, to the [[Boston Celtics]] in exchange for [[Rajon Rondo]] and [[Dwight Powell]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/boston-celtics-complete-trade-dallas-mavericks|title=Boston Celtics Complete Trade With Dallas Mavericks|work=NBA.com|date=December 18, 2014|access-date=December 18, 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150109070550/http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/boston-celtics-complete-trade-dallas-mavericks|archive-date=January 9, 2015}}</ref> In six games for Boston, Nelson averaged 4.8 points and 5.5 assists per game. In his second game with Boston, Nelson returned to Orlando for the first time since leaving for Dallas as a free agent.

===Denver Nuggets (2015–2017)===
On January 13, 2015, Nelson was traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in exchange for [[Nate Robinson]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-acquire-former-all-star-jameer-nelson-boston|title=Nuggets Acquire Former All-Star Jameer Nelson From Boston - Denver Nuggets|website=nba.com|access-date=May 9, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171028045218/http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-acquire-former-all-star-jameer-nelson-boston/|archive-date=October 28, 2017}}</ref> On June 26, 2015, Nelson opted out of the remaining year of his contract with the Nuggets to become a free agent.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.denverpost.com/nuggets/ci_28390311/jameer-nelson-opts-out-contract-denver-nuggets|title=Jameer Nelson opts out of contract with Denver Nuggets|date=June 26, 2015|website=denverpost.com|access-date=May 9, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305090554/http://www.denverpost.com/nuggets/ci_28390311/jameer-nelson-opts-out-contract-denver-nuggets|archive-date=March 5, 2016}}</ref>

On August 7, 2015, Nelson re-signed with the Nuggets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-re-sign-darrell-arthur-will-barton-and-jameer-nelson|title=Nuggets Re-Sign Darrell Arthur, Will Barton and Jameer Nelson|work=NBA.com|date=August 7, 2015|access-date=August 7, 2015|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150810012450/http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-re-sign-darrell-arthur-will-barton-and-jameer-nelson|archive-date=August 10, 2015}}</ref>

On October 18, 2017, Nelson was waived by the Nuggets.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mizell |first=Gina |date=October 18, 2017 |title=Jameer Nelson waived by Nuggets, clearing way for Denver to sign Richard Jefferson |url=http://www.denverpost.com/2017/10/18/jameer-nelson-waived-by-nuggets/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171019010133/http://www.denverpost.com/2017/10/18/jameer-nelson-waived-by-nuggets/ |archive-date=October 19, 2017 |access-date=October 18, 2017 |website=DenverPost.com}}</ref>

[[File:Jameer Nelson (24310641587) (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Nelson with the Pelicans in 2017]]
===New Orleans Pelicans (2017–2018)===
On October 22, 2017, Nelson signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-jameer-nelson|title=Pelicans Sign Jameer Nelson|work=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2017|access-date=October 22, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023071930/http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-jameer-nelson|archive-date=October 23, 2017}}</ref>

===Detroit Pistons (2018)===
On February 1, 2018, Nelson was traded, along with [[Ömer Aşık]], [[Tony Allen (basketball)|Tony Allen]] and a protected first-round pick, to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in exchange for [[Nikola Mirotić]] and a 2018 second-round pick. In addition, Chicago will have the right to swap its 2021 second-round pick with New Orleans' own 2021 second-round pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-acquire-asik-nelson-allen-and-first-round-pick-new-orleans|title=Bulls acquire Asik, Nelson, Allen, and first-round pick from New Orleans|work=NBA.com|date=February 1, 2018|access-date=February 1, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180202072105/http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-acquire-asik-nelson-allen-and-first-round-pick-new-orleans|archive-date=February 2, 2018}}</ref> Seven days later, he was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in exchange for [[Willie Reed]] and future second-round draft considerations.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-acquire-veteran-guard-jameer-nelson|title=Detroit Pistons Acquire Veteran Guard Jameer Nelson|work=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2018|access-date=February 8, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180209071303/http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-acquire-veteran-guard-jameer-nelson|archive-date=February 9, 2018}}</ref>

Nelson's final NBA game was played on March 13, 2018, in a 79–110 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]]. In his final game, Nelson played for 26 minutes and recorded 4 assists, 1 rebound, 1 steal but no points.

==Executive career==
On November 11, 2020, the [[Delaware Blue Coats]] of the [[NBA G League]] named Nelson as the assistant general manager.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jameer Nelson Named Delaware Blue Coats Assistant General Manager |url=https://bluecoats.gleague.nba.com/news/jameer-nelson-named-delaware-blue-coats-assistant-general-manager/ |website=gleague.nba.com |access-date=November 11, 2020 |date=November 11, 2020}}</ref> On May 13, 2025, Nelson was promoted to serve as the assistant general manager for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] under [[Daryl Morey]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=76ers promote former NBA veteran Jameer Nelson to assistant general manager|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/breaking-news/article/76ers-promote-former-nba-veteran-jameer-nelson-to-assistant-general-manager-151823912.html|access-date=August 15, 2025|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}}</ref> On June 7, 2026, after Morey was fired and [[Mike Gansey]] was hired as president of basketball operations, Nelson was promoted to executive vice president of basketball operations.<ref>{{cite web|first=Shams|last=Charania|date=June 7, 2026|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48992547/76ers-promote-jameer-nelson-elton-brand-gm|title=Sources: 76ers promote Jameer Nelson; Elton Brand taking new role|access-date=June 7, 2026|website=NBA.com}}</ref>

==Career statistics==

==Personal life==
On August 30, 2007, Nelson's father, Floyd "Pete" Nelson, was reported missing after disappearing at his Chester [[tugboat]] repair shop located along the docks of the [[Delaware River]] at Front Street and Highland Avenue. Authorities said no one saw his father fall into the water. Nelson arrived at the search scene the next morning. On September 2, 2007, Floyd Nelson's body was found floating in the Delaware River. His death was ruled accidental.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nba_news/jameer_nelson_father_identified.html|title=NBA.com Police: Body is Jameer Nelson's Father|website=www.nba.com|access-date=May 9, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171102234201/http://www.nba.com/nba_news/jameer_nelson_father_identified.html|archive-date=November 2, 2017}}</ref>

He has a tattoo on his back that says ''All Eyes On Me'', and another one that says ''Accomplish Everything Without Fear''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/news/nelsoninterview.html|title=NBA.com - Jameer Nelson Interview From China|website=www.nba.com|access-date=May 9, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714194440/http://www.nba.com/news/nelsoninterview.html|archive-date=July 14, 2014}}</ref>

On July 5, 2008, he married long-time girlfriend, Imani Tillery. He has one son from a previous relationship, [[Jameer Nelson Jr.|Jameer Jr.]], who was a guard for [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/36033839/jameer-nelson-jr-son-ex-nba-guard-transferring-tcu|title=Jameer Nelson Jr., son of ex-NBA guard, transferring to TCU|website=ESPN.com|date=April 2023 |access-date=April 2, 2023}}</ref>
